pr_title: Chore(agent_usage): add agent usage logs for watcher-smoke and other …
verdict: READY TO MERGE - 16 of 16 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: `context_tokens` and `requests` stay out of `required`, so pre-0.7.0 JSONL rows still validate, and the contract test (tests/mods/test_agent_watcher_usage_contract.py:43-64) pins the optional set and both value rules to usageRow.ts.
`requests` minimum 1 with null for unheard matches the writer check at usageRow.ts:240 (positive integer or null) and the tracker, which only emits a count from a non-empty tally.
The top-level description's cost list was updated to name the two new columns, keeping the summary in step with the properties.
The `tokens` redefinition is honest about the in-place semantic change for older rows instead of silently reinterpreting historical data.

The schema and the TypeScript validator are pinned from both sides: test_agent_usage_schema.py rejects negative, fractional and zero values, usageRow.test.ts rejects the same values plus strings, and the contract test ties USAGE_OPTIONAL and the error strings to the schema's type and minimum.
Backward compatibility is tested in both languages: a row without context_tokens and requests still validates, matching the 'older rows lack them' contract.
The tracker tests are behavioral: turn.step is answered by a fake engine stream beneath the real hook, and a pass-through test (lines 506-516) shows the hook changes no chunk and no result.
The 'requests count once' test (468-474) pins the takeTally reset, so a second dispatch under the same loop id cannot reuse the first one's requests.

test_agent_frontmatter_contract.py closes a real gap ('claude plugin validate --strict' skips agent frontmatter keys). It declares WALK_ROOTS correctly and checks omitClaudeMd in both directions, so neither an extra agent nor a missing one passes.
`takeTally` deletes the entry on read, so a reused loop id starts from zero; tracker.test.ts:468-474 pins this behavior.
The `turn.step` hook is a pass-through generator (`yield* next(e)`) that reads usage only after the stream ends, and a test asserts that chunks and the result pass through unchanged.

`foldAgent` uses conditional spreads, so a completion without `contextTokens`/`requests` keeps the stored values; requests add up and the context size follows the latest report, as the `applyCompletion` docstring says.

The `numberProblems` checks for `context_tokens` (>= 0 or null) and `requests` (>= 1 or null) match the schema's `minimum` and nullable types, and `buildUsageRow` always emits both keys, as the `USAGE_OPTIONAL` comment says.
Synchronous loops end in `recordLoopEnd` before the `loopsAtom` lookup returns early, so their tally survives until `recordResult` takes it.
The README's foreground, background and errored token rules (lines 174-180, 253) match recordResult and recordLoopEnd in hooks/core/tracker.ts and the tracker tests at tracker.test.ts:453-503.
The new turn.step hook-table row (README line 197) describes the handler exactly: it reads usage after the stream passes through and skips the main loop (tracker.ts:421-425).
The pre-0.7.0 note ties to the actual manifest bump (0.6.0 to 0.7.0) and to the schema marking context_tokens and requests optional for older rows.

Each of the four omitClaudeMd agents already restates the shell rule and the no-vendor-names rule in its body, and tests/skills/test_agent_frontmatter_contract.py pins both the key set and the restated rules.

The two new columns land in all four places together: agent_usage.schema.json, the TS validator and USAGE_OPTIONAL in usageRow.ts, the Python contract mirror test, and jsonschema tests, with rows lacking both columns still validating.
takeTally removes the tally on read, so a reused loop id starts from zero; tracker.test.ts pins it with two dispatches of the same loop id logging [400, 0].
The turn.step hook is a pure passthrough (yield* next, then tally) and a dedicated test proves every chunk and the result reach the caller unchanged.
The meaning change of foreground `tokens` before 0.7.0 is documented in the README, the usage schema and the matrix schema descriptions, so old rows stay interpretable.
Errored dispatches take and discard their tally before the isDone check, so an error never leaks request counts into a later agent's row, and the test covers it.

The new frontmatter contract test guards a misspelled omitClaudeMd key that strict validation would not catch, requires each omitting agent to restate the rules CLAUDE.md supplied, and declares WALK_ROOTS for test selection.
Committed usage rows from a real run show requests 1 with tokens equal to context_tokens, evidence the turn.step agentId matches the Agent result's agentId in the engine.

The README, the agent_usage schema descriptions, the usageRow.ts USAGE_OPTIONAL comment and the AgentRec/Completion doc comments all describe `tokens` vs `context_tokens` vs `requests` the same way; the Python contract test pins the TS validator messages and null-writing expressions to the schema.
The meaning change of foreground `tokens` is documented in three places (README 187-189, agent_usage `tokens` description, matrix `tokens` description), so readers of old rows know they are mixed.
The `turn.step` hook passes chunks and results through untouched, and a dedicated test (tracker.test.ts:544-554) proves it, which keeps the observer non-invasive.

test_agent_frontmatter_contract.py guards against a silently misspelled `omitClaudeMd`, and checks that every omitting agent restates the shell and vendor-name rules it no longer inherits from CLAUDE.md.
Both plugin versions are bumped alongside their changes (agent-watcher 0.7.0, harness 0.55.1), and the README's 'before 0.7.0' note matches the new version.

minor.name: Token-figure block sits under the Review-local runs heading
minor.summary:
The four new paragraphs defining tokens, context_tokens and requests (lines 169-189) apply to every usage row, foreground and background, claimed or unclaimed, but they sit at the end of the '### Review-local runs' subsection. A reader looking up a usage-row column finds them under a heading about local-<label> run keys, while '## Agent usage rows' (line 244) lists the same columns without their definitions. The block was already misplaced before the PR in a shorter form; the PR quadrupled it in place.

Also (docs): Lines 187-189 say only usage rows' foreground tokens changed meaning at 0.7.0. Matrix rows take the same agent figure (hooks/layers/pr-review/matrixRow.ts:62, tokens: whole(a.tokens)), so a foreground pr-review reviewer's matrix tokens also moved from the last request's count to the summed figure. The matrix schema's tokens description now says this, but the README (R2 at line 97, Matrix-row ownership at 222-242) does not.

Also (overall): The PR is titled 'Chore(agent_usage): add agent usage logs for watcher-smoke and other ...' with body '...skills', but it also ships three feature commits: the `context_tokens` column and the change of foreground `tokens` to the summed request figure (ff16d21), the `requests` column (d123881), and `omitClaudeMd` on four harness agents with a frontmatter contract test (97369bd). The meaning shift of `tokens` for foreground rows is something a log consumer needs to read in the PR.

Also (system_shape): README.md:185 says '`tokens` divided by `requests` is the mean request size'. But `requests` counts every `turn.step`, with or without usage (tracker.ts:73), while a foreground `tokens` sums only the requests that reported usage (tracker.ts:74, 257). The quotient therefore understates the mean whenever a request had no usage. Separately, the schema's `context_tokens` description gives the null cases as 'an errored result, or a background agent none of whose requests the watcher heard'. The code is also null when requests were heard but none reported usage: `tally.last` is undefined (tracker.ts:281), and the 'request with no usage' path in tracker.test.ts:522-528 shows that tallies without `last` are reachable.

Also (system_shape): The PR title is the first commit's 'Chore(agent_usage): add agent usage logs ...' and the body is just '...skills'. The branch also carries Feat(agent-watcher) context_tokens and requests columns (agent-watcher 0.7.0, with a changed meaning for foreground `tokens`) and Feat(agents) `omitClaudeMd: true` on four harness agents (harness 0.55.1). A reader of the merged history gets no hint of the `tokens` meaning change.
fix: Move lines 169-189 to the '## Agent usage rows' section (after the paragraph ending at line 257), so the column list at line 248 and the column definitions sit together.
Give the block its own '### Usage figures' subheading under '## Agent usage rows'.
Extend line 187-189 with: 'Matrix rows follow the same change: a foreground reviewer's matrix tokens before 0.7.0 is its last request's count.'
Add the same note to the R2 row at line 97.
Retitle the PR to cover the agent-watcher 0.7.0 token columns and the omitClaudeMd agents, and write a body listing the three feature commits and the pre-0.7.0 `tokens` meaning note from the README.
README.md:185: qualify the sentence, e.g. '`tokens` divided by `requests` is the mean request size when every request reported usage.'
agent_usage.schema.json `context_tokens.description`: change the null case to '...or a background agent none of whose requests the watcher heard with usage'.

Retitle the PR (e.g. 'Feat(agent-watcher): summed tokens, context_tokens and requests per dispatch; agents omit CLAUDE.md') and give the body one bullet per feature, including the pre-0.7.0 `tokens` meaning note from the README.

minor.name: Background context_tokens null condition is narrower in the prose than in the code
minor.summary: Line 180 says a background row's context_tokens is null when no request was heard on turn.step. In the code, tallyStep (hooks/core/tracker.ts:71-75) sets last only for a request that returned usage, and recordLoopEnd (tracker.ts:281) logs context_tokens only when tally.last is set. A loop whose requests were heard but none carried usage logs requests >= 1 with context_tokens null, a case the README sentence excludes. The schema's context_tokens description has the same wording.
fix: Change line 180 to: '`context_tokens` is the last request heard on `turn.step` that reported usage, null when none did.'
Apply the same wording to the context_tokens description in plugins/harness/schemas/agent_usage.schema.json.

minor.name: Agent usage rows paragraph lists only the background not-measured case and breaks the wrap
minor.summary: Line 253-255 says 'a background turn with no usage logs tokens: 0 ... with usage not measured'. Since this PR a foreground dispatch with no turn.step heard also logs tokens 0 and 'usage not measured' (tracker.ts:257,264; tracker.test.ts:461-465), which line 176 states but this summary paragraph does not. The edited lines 248 and 253 also run to about 150 characters while the rest of the file wraps at 110.
fix: Rewrite line 253-255 as: '... with zero usage and `context_tokens` and `requests` null; a foreground result with no request heard, or a background turn with no usage, logs `tokens: 0` (...) with `usage not measured` in `notes`', and rewrap lines 248 and 253 at 110 characters.

minor.name: Completion.contextTokens docstring contradicts the foreground path
minor.summary:
layer.ts:21 says `contextTokens` is 'absent when no request was heard'. But `recordResult` sets it from the Agent result's `totalTokens` whether or not any request was heard (tracker.ts:258), and the test at tracker.test.ts:461-466 pins `context_tokens: 1000` with no request heard. It is absent only for an errored result or for a background loop with no request that reported usage.

Also (overall): layer.ts documents `contextTokens` as 'Tokens of the last model request alone; absent when no request was heard'. recordResult (tracker.ts:258) sets it from the Agent result's `totalTokens` whether or not any `turn.step` was heard, and tracker.test.ts:499-503 pins exactly that case (no request heard, context_tokens 1000). The doc only holds for the background path (tally.last).
fix: Reword layer.ts:21 to: `/** Tokens of the last model request alone; absent when unknown (an errored result, or a background loop with no request reporting usage). */`
Reword layer.ts:25 to: 'Tokens of the last model request alone (foreground: the result's totalTokens; background: the last request heard on turn.step); absent when unknown.'

minor.name: Step tallies leak for loops whose Agent result is never folded
minor.summary:
The `turn.step` hook (tracker.ts:421-425) tallies every subagent request into `stepTallies`, but an entry is removed only by `takeTally`, which runs in `recordResult` for a non-error result (line 254, `res` is undefined when `r.isError === true`, so `res?.agentId` is undefined) and in `recordLoopEnd` only after the loop is found in `loopsAtom` (line 278). Three paths never take the tally: an errored synchronous dispatch (the test at tracker.test.ts:499-504 steps loop-x and then errors, leaving loop-x in the map), any Agent dispatch outside a harness project (the `tool.call` hook returns `next(e)` at line 399 without reaching `recordResult`), and a background loop not registered in `loopsAtom`. Each such loop leaves an entry in the module-level map for the life of the process. The old `toolUses` map does not have this problem because it is deleted before the `hit` check (line 275). The leak is small per entry but unbounded, and a later completion under a reused loop id would inherit the stale requests and tokens.

Also (overall): The `turn.step` hook tallies every subagent request (tracker.ts:421-425) in any project, but a tally is only removed by recordResult (line 254) or by recordLoopEnd after a registered loop is found (line 278). Outside a harness project trackedDispatch returns undefined (line 399), so neither runs; an untracked background loop also returns at line 277 before takeTally. Each such loop leaves one module-level map entry for the life of the process. Small per entry, but unbounded across a long session in a non-harness project where the mod is installed globally.

Also (system_shape): The map's doc (tracker.ts:64) says a tally is 'taken when the loop's agent completes', and the module header claims state stays bounded. In practice three paths never call takeTally. (1) An errored or denied Agent result: `res` is undefined (line 250), so `takeTally(res?.agentId)` at line 254 takes nothing. (2) A dispatch outside a harness project: the Agent hook returns `next(e)` at line 399 without reaching recordResult. (3) A background loop that was never registered: recordLoopEnd returns at line 277 before takeTally at line 278. Meanwhile the `turn.step` hook (lines 421-425) tallies every subagent loop unconditionally, so those entries pile up for the whole process. Because the map lives at module level, the tracker tests also share it: the errored-dispatch test (tracker.test.ts:501) leaves a `loop-x` tally behind, and the next `loop-x` dispatch would fold that leftover in if the runner keeps module state between tests. The toolUses map does not have this problem because it is deleted before the hit check (line 275).
fix: In `recordResult`, take the tally from the raw result whatever its status: `const tally = takeTally((r.result as AgentResult | undefined)?.agentId)`, kept after the `async_launched` return, so errored results also clear their entry.
In the `tool.call` Agent hook's untracked branch (tracker.ts:399), await `next(e)`, call `takeTally` on the result's `agentId`, and return the result.

In the untracked branch of the Agent hook (tracker.ts:399), await next(e) and call takeTally on the result's agentId for a synchronous result; for an untracked `async_launched` result, remember the loop id in a small set and drop its tally (and the set entry) in recordLoopEnd when `hit` is undefined.
Alternatively, skip tallying in the `turn.step` hook when the session has no harness project (resolve the watch once and cache the answer per process).

In recordResult, take the tally for the dispatched loop even when the result is errored or denied (key it from the dispatch, not from `res`). In the untracked branch at line 399, drop the tally for the result's agentId. In recordLoopEnd, when `hit` is undefined, mark the loop id as ended so the next main-loop `turn.complete` can delete tallies of ended, unregistered loops.
Bound stepTallies: keep it as an insertion-ordered Map and evict the oldest entries past a fixed cap. Fix the doc at tracker.ts:64 to match whichever rule is chosen.

minor.name: Foreground row is marked measured when no heard request reported usage
minor.summary: `recordResult` sets `isMeasured: isDone && tally !== undefined` (tracker.ts:264). `tallyStep` creates a tally on any request, including one whose `usage` is null (line 74 keeps `sum` at 0 and leaves `last` unset). A foreground agent whose heard requests all lack usage therefore logs `tokens: 0` with notes that claim the usage was measured. The docstring at lines 238-242 ties 'not measured' to 'no request heard', and the background path ties it to whether usage arrived (`e.usage !== undefined`, line 284), so the two paths judge measurement differently.
fix: Gate measurement on reported usage: `isMeasured: isDone && tally?.last !== undefined`, and update the docstring to read 'With no request reporting usage, its tokens are 0 and not measured.'

minor.name: Background row drops the heard request sum when the loop turn carries no usage
minor.summary:
`recordLoopEnd` takes `tokens` only from `e.usage` (tracker.ts:281) and sets `isMeasured: e.usage !== undefined` (line 284). When `turn.complete` has no usage but the tally summed reported requests, the row logs `tokens: 0` and 'usage not measured' even though `tally.sum` is known and is already logged as `context_tokens`/`requests`. The foreground path uses `tally.sum` for the same figure, so the two paths are inconsistent.

Also (overall): A foreground row takes `tokens` from the summed `turn.step` tally (tracker.ts:257), but a background row takes it only from `turn.complete` usage (line 281) and marks the row unmeasured when that is absent (line 284), even when the tally holds a summed figure and `contextTokens`/`requests` from the same tally are logged on that row. The row then reports `tokens: 0`, `usage not measured` beside a non-null `context_tokens` and `requests`, a figure the mod already measured.
fix: Fall back to the tally: `tokens: e.usage !== undefined ? usageTokens(e.usage) : (tally?.sum ?? 0)` and `isMeasured: e.usage !== undefined || tally?.last !== undefined`, and note the fallback in the docstring at lines 269-272.

In recordLoopEnd, use `e.usage` when present, else `tally.sum` when `tally?.last !== undefined`, and set `isMeasured` true in either case; update the README Background bullet and the schema `tokens` description to say so, and add a tracker test with steps heard and a loop end without usage.
Or keep the behavior and state in the README Background bullet that `tokens` is 0 when `turn.complete` carries no usage even though `context_tokens` and `requests` were heard.

minor.name: Matrix test title claims every reviewer row is measured; r2 is now unmeasured
minor.summary:
The test 'one measured row per reviewer once the review has a verdict' seeds one request for loop-x (line 208), then dispatches r1 and r2, both answered by a completed result with agentId loop-x. recordResult takes the tally for r1 (tracker.ts:254 takeTally), so r2 finds no tally: tokens 0, isMeasured false, and its matrix row notes read 'usage not measured (session restarted mid-run)' (matrixRow.ts:51), a cause that did not happen. The test asserts only rows[0], so the title's 'one measured row per reviewer' is false for the second row and nothing pins it.

Also (overall): Both reviewer results share agentId `loop-x`; the test seeds one tally (line 208), which r1's result takes, so r2 is logged with tokens 0 and unmeasured. Only rows[0] is asserted, so the test name no longer describes what runs and r2's measured path is not covered.

Also (system_shape): The test 'one measured row per reviewer once the review has a verdict' calls `steps($, seen, 'loop-x', 1000)` once, then dispatches r1 and r2, and both results carry agentId `loop-x`. r1 takes the tally. r2 finds none, so it logs tokens 0 with isMeasured false. The test only asserts on rows[0], so its title no longer describes the second row it produces.
fix: Add `await steps($, seen, 'loop-x', 1000)` before `dispatch($, reviewerPrompt('r2'))` and assert `rows[1]` has `tokens: 1000` as well.
Or retitle the test to say only the first reviewer is measured and assert rows[1] is `tokens: 0` with the not-measured note.
Add `await steps($, seen, 'loop-x', 1000)` between the two dispatches (tracker.test.ts:209-210) and assert `rows[1]` has `tokens: 1000` as well.
Or rename the test to drop 'measured'.
Add a second `steps($, seen, 'loop-x', 1000)` between the two dispatches, so each reviewer's loop has requests, and assert `rows[1]` has tokens 1000.
Rename the test to drop 'measured' (e.g. 'one row per reviewer once the review has a verdict; attempted once').

minor.name: Foreground test cannot tell totalTokens from the last request
minor.summary: The test titled 'context_tokens is the result's totalTokens' feeds loop-x requests 300 and 1000, and the completed result reports totalTokens 1000. The last request and totalTokens are the same number, so a regression that logged the last step's tally (as the background path does) for a foreground agent would still pass. Line 461's no-request test covers the totalTokens source only when no step was heard.
fix: Use step totals whose last differs from 1000, e.g. `steps($, seen, 'loop-x', 300, 400)` and expect `{ tokens: 700, context_tokens: 1000, requests: 2 }`.

minor.name: 'adds no tokens' is asserted on a path that ignores the tally sum
minor.summary: The test 'a request with no usage counts as a request and adds no tokens' runs a background launch, where tokens come from the loop turn's usage (tracker.ts:281 usageTokens(e.usage)), never from tally.sum. tokens 40 equals the loopEnd total whatever the null request contributes, so the 'adds no tokens' half of the title cannot fail. The sum is only read on the foreground path (tracker.ts:257).
fix: Add a foreground case: `steps($, seen, 'loop-x', 40, null)`, dispatch a completed result, and expect `{ tokens: 40, requests: 2 }`.
Or drop 'adds no tokens' from the title and keep the background assertions for count and last usage.

minor.name: Errored-dispatch test seeds a loop tally and never shows it discarded
minor.summary: The test seeds a loop-x request of 500 and dispatches an errored result. recordResult reads the loop id from the result (tracker.ts:250,254), and an errored result has none, so takeTally(undefined) leaves the loop-x tally in the module-level stepTallies map. The test asserts the nulls on the row but not what happens to that tally. A later agent that reuses the loop id would pick up the 500, and in a long session errored foreground loops build up in the map. Nothing pins either behavior.
fix: After the errored dispatch, dispatch a completed result under loop-x with no new steps and assert `tokens: 0, requests: null`. That shows whether the tally leaks, and if it does, clear tallies for loops that end with no registered launch once their result is known.
Or document in the test that the stale tally is accepted because loop ids are unique, and add a size bound on stepTallies in tracker.ts.

minor.name: Schemas README update protocol not followed for two changed schemas
minor.summary: plugins/harness/schemas/README.md:270 states: 'When changing any schema file under this directory, update this README in the SAME PR.' This PR changes agent_usage.schema.json (adds the `context_tokens` and `requests` columns, and redefines `tokens`) and pr_review_invocation_test_matrix.schema.json (redefines `tokens`), but leaves the README untouched. Neither schema has an entry in its Files list (sections 1-8), so the drift predates this PR, but the PR's schema change is exactly what the protocol covers.
fix: Add Files entries for `agent_usage.schema.json` (one row per Agent dispatch; columns including `tokens` summed, `context_tokens` last request, `requests`; writer agent-watcher) and `pr_review_invocation_test_matrix.schema.json` to plugins/harness/schemas/README.md.

minor.name: tokens description names the semantic split but not how to detect an old row
minor.summary: The `tokens` description says rows written before agent-watcher 0.7.0 hold, for a foreground dispatch, the last request's count. A row carries no version field; the only discriminator is the presence of the `context_tokens` key, which is stated in that column's description (line 84) but not here, where a consumer summing `tokens` (e.g. tools/harness_usage_charts.py:95) would look.
fix: Append to the `tokens` description: `A row without the `context_tokens` key predates 0.7.0.`

minor.name: context_tokens null cases understate when the writer emits null
minor.summary: The description says `context_tokens` is null for an errored result or a background agent none of whose requests the watcher heard. The writer is null in two more cases: a background agent whose requests were heard but none carried usage (tracker.ts:74 sets `last` only when usage is present, and tracker.ts:281 omits contextTokens when `tally.last` is undefined, while `requests` is still a positive count), and a completed foreground agent whose result lacks `totalTokens` (tracker.ts:258). A reader of the schema would wrongly infer that a non-null `requests` implies a non-null `context_tokens`.
fix: Reword the null clause to: `Null when unknown (an errored result, a foreground result without a total, or an agent none of whose requests reported usage).`

minor.name: Matrix rows give no way to tell pre-0.7.0 tokens from the new summed figure
minor.summary:
The `tokens` description now says rows the agent-watcher wrote before 0.7.0 hold, for a foreground dispatch, the last request's count instead of the summed count. Unlike agent_usage (where the presence of `context_tokens` marks a 0.7.0+ row), a matrix row has no column that dates it or names the writer version: `additionalProperties` is false, there is no `logged_at`, and `dev_commit` anchors the reviewed project's merge base, not the watcher. A rollup over the matrix therefore mixes the two meanings of `tokens` with nothing to separate them, and the caveat in the description cannot be acted on.

Also (system_shape): The new `tokens` description in pr_review_invocation_test_matrix.schema.json says the value is summed over every model request of the invocation. The same matrix is also written by pr-team-orchestrator Step 5 when no `.matrix_owner` marker exists (pr-team-orchestrator.md:375-391). That path derives `tokens` from the reviewer output file's metadata block, or uses 0, and cannot produce a per-request sum. The schema now asserts a meaning that one of its two writers does not follow.
fix: Add an optional marker column the matrix writer (plugins/agent-watcher/hooks/layers/pr-review/matrixRow.ts) emits from 0.7.0 on, e.g. `context_tokens` (integer or null, same meaning as in agent_usage), and state in the `tokens` description that a row without it may hold the older last-request figure.
Or state in the `tokens` description how a consumer identifies older rows (for example by joining on agent_usage via `cell`/`pr`), if such a join exists.

Extend the schema description: 'Rows the agent-watcher mod writes: ... summed over every model request. Rows the pr-team orchestrator writes without the mod (Step 5) carry the reviewer's self-reported figure, or 0.'
Align pr-team-orchestrator.md Step 5 so its `tokens` bullet names the same meaning, or states the difference.

minor.name: Contract module docstring left with ragged line breaks
minor.summary:
The edit to the module docstring splits the sentence into lines ending 'the skill and' and 'the model family enum,', which are much shorter than the 110 width the rest of the docstring fills. It reads as an unfinished reflow.

Also (overall): The edited docstring breaks mid-sentence at 'counts, the skill and' / 'role patterns, the model family enum,' leaving short ragged lines inside a paragraph wrapped at 110 elsewhere.

Also (system_shape): The module docstring of test_agent_watcher_usage_contract.py breaks one sentence over lines 6-8 at uneven points ('counts, the skill and' / 'role patterns, the model family enum,'), unlike the 110-column wrap of the surrounding lines.
fix: Reflow lines 5-9 into full-width lines, e.g. '``fields`` object and its key, length and no-path rules, the optional ``context_tokens`` and ``requests`` counts, the skill and role patterns, the model family enum, ``logged_at`` pattern, nullable strings or non-empty strings without the mod following.'
Reflow lines 3-9 of the module docstring to the file's usual width with no content change.
Reflow lines 4-9 of the docstring to the 110-column width.
